a Gore-Tex spray-suit was protective in orchard pesticide applications.

the development of an experimental Gore-Tex suit for use in pesticide spraying, with the determination of its protective value, and with the determination of how much pesticide actually gets on the body.
the development of a new method for the measurement of the protective properties of spray suits.
the protection provided by a Gore-Tex spray jacket and pants, and a commercial poly-vinyl chloride (PVC) suit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two suits were equally protective in a fungicide orchard spray.
the two spray suits were equally protective of the upper body in orchard spraying.
the Gore-Tex suit was as protective of the body as the polyvinylchlorid suit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spray suits are protective but that deposition is variable.
spray suits provide substantial protection against spray drift, but the degree of protection is highly variable.
spray suits are protective and that the Gore-Tex and polyvinylchlorides are equally protective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a spray suit can substantially reduce pesticide exposure.
a well designed and fitted suit, whether made of Gore-Tex or PVC, can protect the worker from pesticide spray drift, even in orchard spraying.
spray suits are effective in reducing pesticide deposition on the body, and the effectiveness is not dependent on the fabric of the suit.
